From LMSYS-Chat-1M take English first-user turns of at most 200 input tokens, remove duplicates and known detectable benchmark overlap, then use a fixed shuffled candidate order. The two unmodified R1-distill-Qwen models each generate their own single clean response to the same candidate prompt. Retain shared IDs only if both outputs satisfy the predeclared reasoning/finalanswer, finish-reason and sequence-length checks. The target is 10,000 accepted paired training prompt IDs plus 100 separate validation IDs, not merely 10,000 raw candidates. Clean traces are cached before any transformation [44, 39].

The clean generation policy is temperature 0.6, top-p = 0.95, up to 3,072 new tokens, no added system prompt and native reasoning formatting. The whole prompt-plus-transformed-answer must fit the 4,096-token SFT context bound across all strengths for the relevant tokenizer. Parsing failures, absent reasoning, cutoff completions and exclusions are saved rather than silently discarded. The common accepted prompt IDs do not imply that the two model sizes have identical clean traces. The accepted set is reasoning-eligible LMSYS-derived data, not a representative random sample of all LMSYS interactions.

The selected count of 10,000 is a fixed resource-risk compromise, not a sample-complexity theorem or a guarantee of sufficient training exposure. The closest ROT13 work used approximately 85,500 traces; ciphered-reasoning training on a mathematical corpus has also used 16,000 source problems expanded into multiple examples per problem [44, 46]. Full reasoning and accounting appear in Appendix B.1.4.

SFT source generation uses fresh vLLM responses from separate pinned 7B and 14B workers on H100 80-GB Pods, in chunks of 128 requests. Every request retains its full 3072-new-token allowance; batching does not divide this cap. Use BF16 weights without quantization, native prompt token IDs and EOS IDs, and independent per-example seeds. Archive old native and benchmark outputs; do not mix them into training. Save and verify each whole batch in Google Drive before advancing. Initial raw generation is followed by joint acceptance and exact-deficit refills using new ordered IDs.

Approved conservative statistical confidence guard
patches.text:
H.8.3 Maximum-standardized lower bounds with a design-based concentration guard

The paired, design-aware bootstrap still uses 10,000 draws. For each scalar metric j, retain its observed estimate theta_j, bootstrap standard error s_j and full-family critical value q = max(0, higher empirical 95th percentile of max_j[(theta*_j - theta_j)/s_j]). The original bootstrap lower bound is theta_j - q*s_j, clipped to its natural range. It is retained separately for diagnosis.

Approved revision, 11 October 2026: the original method failed mandatory coverage validation. Before any trained outcomes were inspected, the user authorized a more conservative confidence-bound construction conditional on leaving SFT unchanged. The reported lower bound is now the smaller of the original bootstrap lower bound and a simultaneous design-concentration ratio lower bound. This changes only evaluation uncertainty; all training data, loss, optimizer, epochs, scientific success floors, evaluation IDs and Monte Carlo acceptance rules remain unchanged.

For bounded item outcomes, SRS without replacement has a moment bound no larger than independent sampling from the same finite population. Combine independent strata using their fixed allocation weights; exact censuses contribute zero variation. Nested non-MMLU legibility subsets are marginal SRS from the original stratum. MMLU capability retains all 57 fixed subject strata. Its legibility calculation separately bounds selected single-question errors and selection of 50 of 57 subject means.

For T allocated questions, Vq = sum(n_h/T^2) over noncensus question strata. The separate MMLU subject contribution is Vs = m/T^2 when m subjects are selected from S and m < S, otherwise zero. A bounded component in [a,b] has one-sided radius (b-a)*r, where r = sqrt(log(2/delta)*Vq/2) + sqrt(log(2/delta)*Vs/2). Each stage receives delta/2. Allocate delta = 0.05/(3*p) to each numerator-lower, denominator-upper and denominator-lower component across the complete p = 10,800-gate family.

Clip component bounds to their natural ranges. Divide a nonnegative numerator lower bound by the denominator upper bound. For a negative numerator lower bound, use the denominator lower bound; if zero, use the ratio's natural lower bound. The union bound protects the complete family, including common-correct ratios and paired differences, without assuming independent gates. No hypotheses or windows are deleted.

Success floors remain 0.80 for per-level retention, 0.60 for common retention, 0.50 for absolute qualified opacity and 0.20 for paired increases. A fixed nonmath-domain pair must pass full and common-correct checks throughout the window. Undefined denominators, missing evidence and unsupported bootstrap variance retain natural-range lower bounds and explicit indeterminate status. The guard can reduce inferential power; it does not alter SFT efficacy or certify a trained model.

H.8.4 Mandatory simulation preflight

Freeze the revised implementation and validation plan before trained outcome inspection. All seven mandatory finite-population scenarios, 100 repetitions each and 10,000 bootstrap draws per repetition remain required. Each scenario must clear the unchanged one-sided 95% Wilson lower coverage bound of 0.95, with no structural failures. Historical failed reports cannot certify the revised method. Full mathematical conventions and the sampling-comparison reference are recorded in docs/statistical_concentration_guard.md.

patches.subject: Published efficient SFT baseline and fixed hyperparameters
patches.text:
C.2.1 Published-method baseline and scientific scope

The active efficient_one_epoch_v1 recipe is a newly declared scientific baseline, not an exact migration of NF4 checkpoints. It applies to any explicitly selected model/family/level. All forty datasets remain available; active SFT selects20 14B conditions,both families/all ten levels. Retain7B history. Completedfresh 14B ROT13 L10 retained; all ten14B ROT13 fits complete; tenKaziText conditions uncompleted; $240 SFT authorized 13 Oct. Both families use the same full-target completion-only objective and seeded exposure per chosen fit.

Precedent: LoRA (arxiv.org/abs/2106.09685) supports frozen-base low-rank adaptation. Mixed-precision training (1710.03740) supports lower-precision computation with stable accumulation. FlashAttention (2205.14135) motivates memory-efficient exact attention, used here through standard PyTorch SDPA preference rather than a claimed observed kernel. Cut Cross-Entropy (2411.09009; Apple's upstream implementation) avoids the large vocabulary logits matrix. QLoRA (2305.14314) is a memory-saving precedent, not evidence that NF4 maximizes training throughput. The uploaded one-epoch notebook motivates short exploratory exposure but does not validate 14B runtime or equal final efficacy.

C.2.2 Declared efficient hyperparameters

Objective: completion-only supervised loss on transformed reasoning plus the unchanged final answer; mean supervised-token loss per example, then mean examples. Prompt/padding tokens receive no direct loss.
Base and head: unquantized frozen BF16 weights; BF16 frozen classifier, FP32 dot accumulation with BF16 logits rounding, FP32 loss/hidden-gradient accumulation through exact direct CCE.
LoRA: rank 8, alpha 16, dropout .05; q_proj,k_proj,v_proj,o_proj,gate_proj,up_proj,down_proj. Embeddings/head remain frozen; adapters and optimizer states FP32.
Learning rate/optimizer:2e-4, plain AdamW, zero weight decay, maximum gradient norm.3.
Exposure: one epoch/all 10,000 training records, plus100 distinct validation IDs for diagnostics. Effective16 from requested microbatch2/accumulation8, capacity fallback1/16;625 updates, full cosine horizon 625 and warmup 19.
Sequence policy: maximum 4096 total tokens, no truncation, packing or omitted targets. Seed42.
Attention: standard SDPA preferring flash/efficient implementations; math fallback permitted. Actual selected kernel is not instrumented or claimed.
Memory: policy v2 duplicate-longest guard tries2/off,1/off,2/on,1/on; only CUDA OOM permits fallback. Record batch/accumulation/recomputation mode; exact resume cannot change it. Each ordered16-example update keeps weight1/16 per example; grouping/dropout/rounding differ. No measured gain.
Checkpoints: every 100 updates and final 625; atomic full state, verified Drive publication.

This changes epochs, base/head precision, optimizer and execution relative to the historical two-epoch NF4 recipe. Numerical accumulation fidelity does not prove identical full-fit outcomes. Legacy recipes remain available explicitly and cannot share relabelled checkpoints. Final test panels and original construction/evaluation thresholds remain unchanged.
